docs.text: Not good, folks: We just had the warmest U.S. winter on record. As .bsky.social writes, "Snow cover was scarce, the Great Lakes were mostly ice-free, and a million-acre wildfire tore across Texas."
It’s always strange when a major winter weather event mostly skips the Great Lakes region.
And I actually think that those of us on the West Coast are going to have to develop a similar culture to fire that people in the third coast/Great Lakes have around snow.
All this snow will eventually melt and fuel our amazing waterfalls before replenishing the Great Lakes watershed, so not all bad lol
Also snow and freezing rain across the Great Lakes and beyond.
Interesting because winter just very much pummeled the great lakes region in the us.

The warmest winter in U.S. history leaves its mark. Snow cover was scarce, the Great Lakes were mostly ice-free, and a million-acre wildfire tore across Texas. Read what the excellent Yale Climate Connections has to say about the worsening #ClimateCrisis....

: Much of the Great Lakes region has looked bare almost all winter. The lack of snow and lake ice has left some Midwesterners who ski, skate and fish to question how their lifestyles will persist as the world warms.

"It’s been an almost unrelentingly warm winter, with by far the lowest snow coverage for this time of year ever recorded (13.8% of the lower 48 US states, compared to an average of more than 40%) and the Great Lakes essentially free of ice."...

Anybody old enough to remember what the winter of 1977 was like in the northeastern and Great Lakes part of the United States can understand how this was not a great look at the time. Poor Jimmy. Not the greatest president, but a great human being.
